root_causes.description: The cart service is the dominant anomaly: its container working set averages ~93MB and peaks at ~108MB, roughly 4x peer services (~24-25MB for checkout and product-catalog), while CPU (~0.035) and error rate (0.0) stay low and container recreation events occur. This memory-pressure signature matches a memory_stress fault injected on cart.

evidence.expected_baseline: healthy peer service working set in otel-demo
healthy peer service working set in otel-demo
low CPU rules out cpu_stress as the dominant fault
no error spike rules out http_abort as the dominant fault

evidence.observed_value: Created: Container created (count=2); Started: Container started (count=2)
evidence.expected_baseline: no container recreation during a steady-state window

root_causes.description: Container recreation events (Created/Started count=2) and a restart increase (max ~1.03 over 5m) in the cart pod are consistent with pod instability secondary to memory pressure, but there are no OOMKilled or BackOff events, so this is a weaker explanation than memory_stress.

evidence.observed_value: Created: Container created (count=2); Started: Container started (count=2)

root_causes.description: The injected memory pressure on cart can translate into elevated p99 latency as the container struggles under memory load, but cart shows no error spike and CPU remains low, so latency is a secondary effect rather than the primary fault.

remediation_steps: Disable the cart memory_stress fault via the fault-injection control plane (flagd) for the seed42 scenario.
Raise the cart pod memory requests/limits and investigate a possible memory leak, since the cart working set (~93-108MB) ran ~4x its peer services (~24MB).
Confirm container recreation/restart events subside after the fault is disabled and monitor cart working set returning toward the ~24MB peer baseline.
